issues.detail: Error handling is thin: the Python helper does not handle network errors, timeouts, or invalid JSON bodies, and there is no guidance for retries, redirects, rate limiting (429), or non-JSON responses.

scenarios.name: debug-expired-token-401
scenarios.rationale: Both give a diagnostic plan without actually running tests, but A explicitly includes a no-auth baseline request, a masked token display (last4), an expiry check with refresh guidance, and a GET vs POST comparison, covering more of the rubric's separated cases and the mask requirement, while B lacks a no-auth case, never shows a refreshed-token test, and doesn't mask the token display beyond length.

scenarios.name: users-crud-chain-with-report
scenarios.rationale: A meets the core requirements (30s timeout, id extracted from POST and used in GET/PUT/DELETE, final 404 verification, slow flag over 2s, per-step PASS/FAIL with N/N summary) with minor weaknesses like aborting without cleanup; B uses a 15s timeout instead of 30s, never flags slow responses, uses PATCH rather than PUT, and crashes on network errors, though it does have the 404 check and N/N summary.

scenarios.name: graphql-200-with-errors
scenarios.rationale: A satisfies all rubric points: POST with JSON body and Content-Type, token read from env var, explicit check that errors is absent/empty plus separate data validation, and a 30s timeout; B has no 30s timeout (uses 20s), does not read the token from an env var by default (only optional header), though it does check errors and data separately.
